full_judgment:
Amirul Kabir Chowdhury J: Accused petitioners S.M. Firoj and six others seek leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 02.02.2006 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellance Case No. 8450 of 2005 making the rule absolute. 

 2. On 08.02.2004 one Md. Rafiqul Islam Talukder lodged First Information Report with Naldanga Police Station, district- Natore against the accused petitioners and others stating, inter-alia, that on 07.02.2004 at about 5.30 P.M. while his son Subbir Ahmed Gama along with Ala Uddin @ Alai son of Dubai Khan and others were talking to each other at Rampar, Kazipur, then the accused along with others being armed with deadly weapons formed themselves into unlawful assembly and attacked his son and others and accused Akbar fired from pistol which hit his son and his son was trying to escape and then co-accused Zahirul Assaulted him with sharp cutting weapon and some other accused also assaulted his son who succumbed to the injuries. On the basis of the aforesaid FIR Naldanga Police Station Case No.1 dated 08.02.2004 was started under Section 302 and other Sections of the Penal Code. After investigation police submitted charge sheet against the accused petitioners and others on 15.06.2004. The case was registered as Druto Bichar Tribunal Case No. 26 of 2005 and was pending before learned Druto Bichar Tribunal, Rajshahi. The accused petitioners filed an application under Section 526 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the High Court Division praying to transfer the aforesaid Druto Bichar Tribunal Case No. 26 of 2005 from the court of Druto Bichar Tribunal, Rajshahi to any other Druto Bichar Tribunal, Dhaka, on the basis of which in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 8450 of 2005 rule was issued. The rule was fixed for hearing on 2nd February 2006 while none was present on behalf of the petitioners to press the rule. The learned Judges of the High Court Division heard the learned Deputy Attorney General representing the State who submitted candidly that the State have no objection to transfer the case as prayed for. 

 3. The High Court Division after hearing the learned Deputy Attorney General made the rule absolute allowing the prayer of the accused petitioner and thus withdrew the case and transferred it to Judge of Druto Bichar Tribunal No.3, Dhaka directing to dispose of the case expeditiously. 

 "For that the High Court Division on passing the order of transfer of the case from one tribunal to another tribunal has gone contrary to Section 4(4) of the Ain and as it is liable to be set aside. 

 For that in view of the facts that earlier the High Court Division having passed order in consonance to with Section 4(4) of the Ain and the Appellate Division having issued leave and the same being pending the instant case should be kept pending till disposal of the Criminal Leave to Appeal No. 36 of 2004. 

 For that in view of the fact that jurisdiction of the tribunal to try a case being determined by the Government under Section 5 of the Ain, the instant transfer going contrary to the said provision of law has not been passed in accordance of the provision of the 'Ain'. 

 " Wherefore, it is most humbly prayed that your Lordships would graciously be pleased to issue a Rule calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Rajshahi to show cause as to why the transferring of the Druto Bichar Tribunal Case No. 26 of 2005 (arising out of Naldanga Police Station case No.1, dated 08.02.2004 and G.R. No. 61 of 2004) from the court of learned Druto Bichar Tribunal, Rajshajhi to any other Druto Bichar Tribunal at Dhaka having similar jurisdiction call for the records cause shown, if any and after hearing the parties and perusal of the record making the rule absolute and/or pass such other or further order or orders as your Lordships may deem fit and proper. 

 9. On perusal of the aforesaid prayer it appears that the accused petitioners themselves prayed for transferring the case from the Court of Druto Bichar Tribunal, Rajshahi to any other Druto Bichar Tribunal at Dhaka. From the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division it appears that the case in question has been transferred accordingly to Druto Bichar Tribunal No.3 at Dhaka.
